sources.scope: EER 2026–27 Articles 3.6–3.9 and Appendix I. Controls the core, general education, approved concentrations, projects and Capstone.
Official identity, English full-time bachelor, and interdisciplinary orientation.
Official curriculum overview and named areas of interest, academic core, skills, projects and Capstone.
Official academic motivation, interdisciplinary inquiry and problem-based teaching.
Official 2026–27 UCM catalogue. Core course and skills descriptions, credit conventions, progression and examples from each domain.

curriculum: The single-domain example is 180 EC. Appendix I controls the four named 5 EC courses and the 7.5 and 5 EC core projects. Three 2.5 EC core skills trainings complete the 20 EC skills-and-project allocation. The remaining components are 15 general education, 75 concentration courses, 15 concentration skills, 15 concentration projects and 20 Capstone. General education spans both outside domains in this example. An approved interdisciplinary concentration instead has 5–10 EC in the third domain. Article 3.9 limits introductory concentration courses to 20 EC and requires at least 20 advanced EC across at least three courses, and one advanced concentration project.
progression: Catalogue SKI1004 and SKI1005 develop research questions and then a feasible proposal and qualitative techniques for PRO1012. Academic Skills I and II train academic writing and argument in the first year. The 20 EC Capstone begins only after at least 140 EC. The catalogue also lists COR1006 as core and retains some references to it, but Appendix I specifically enumerates the four mandatory courses and names COR1007, also present in the 2026–27 catalogue.
components: Liberal Arts and Sciences Education in the 21st Century
This example uses three courses (15 EC) across the two domains outside a single concentration. The approved two-domain route instead requires one or two courses in the third domain.
This example uses fifteen courses (75 EC) in one domain. Concentration study combines introductory, intermediate and advanced work, including at least 20 EC of advanced coursework.
